findings.description: listHandler returns Prisma availability, whose weekdays are numbers. Declaring days as string[] makes ListSchedulesPlatformWrapper's getScheduleListItemData(schedule) call incompatible with that transformer's days: number[] parameter, producing TS2345 during type checking. Preserve days: number[] in the copied response type.
findings.failureMode: ListSchedulesPlatformWrapper fails type checking at getScheduleListItemData
findings.title: Use numeric weekdays in the availability response

findings.description: The server response uses IFromUser.id: number, but SlotInfo declares it as string. EventTypeCalendarViewComponent passes useAvailableSlots().data to useAvailableTimeSlots, which still requires IGetAvailableSlots with a numeric fromUser.id; this now fails type checking. Change the local fromUser.id back to number.
findings.failureMode: Calendar view fails type checking when passing the locally typed response to the shared slot hook
findings.title: Preserve the numeric out-of-office source ID

findings.description: The new @calcom/trpc/** restriction rejects existing QueryCell imports in ConferencingAppsViewPlatformWrapper.tsx and SelectedCalendarsSettingsPlatformWrapper.tsx. Running Biome lint on atoms now fails for these files. Move or replace those imports before enabling the broader restriction.
findings.failureMode: Atoms lint fails on existing QueryCell imports
findings.title: Migrate the remaining imports before broadening the ban

findings.description: The new ./booker/types export targets ./booker/types.ts, but the package files allowlist ships only dist, globals.min.css, and fonts. Published consumers importing @calcom/atoms/booker/types cannot resolve the advertised module. Target an emitted declaration in dist or include the source file in the published package.
findings.failureMode: Published package cannot resolve newly advertised booker/types subpath
findings.title: Ship the file targeted by the new types export

findings.description: The former Slot definition and getSlots return type use userIds?: number[], but the local copy changes it to string[]. An existing onTimeslotsLoaded callback typed with numeric slot IDs is now incompatible with BookerPlatformWrapperAtomProps, so integrations that previously type-checked fail to compile. Keep userIds as number[] when moving the type.
findings.failureMode: Existing callbacks using the numeric Slot contract fail TypeScript assignment
findings.title: Preserve numeric IDs in the moved Slot type

findings.description: validateCreateScheduleInput accepts {name: "x", schedule: 123, eventTypeId: "invalid"} and returns it as CreateScheduleInput because only name is checked. Callers therefore receive a successfully validated value whose optional fields violate the promised type. Validate all fields with a local typed Zod schema before returning.
findings.failureMode: Invalid optional fields pass the new input validator
findings.title: Validate optional schedule fields before casting

findings.description: Replacing the previous `.encode('unicode_escape').decode('utf-8')` transformation with raw keyword escaping breaks searches over serialized workflow inputs/outputs. The default execution repository still uses json.dumps with ensure_ascii=True, so an input '你好' is stored as '\u4f60\u597d'; the new '%你好%' pattern returns no matching logs. Preserve JSON encoding before LIKE escaping for these fields, separately from the plain-text session-ID pattern.
findings.failureMode: Workflow log keyword search no longer finds serialized Unicode input/output values.
findings.title: Preserve JSON encoding when searching workflow inputs and outputs

findings.description: The connection sets cz.sql.string.literal.escape.mode='quote', where backslashes are literal, but this f-string emits ESCAPE '\\' (two backslashes). SQL LIKE requires a single escape character, so the fallback query fails even for ordinary keywords. Emit a single backslash SQL literal in quote mode.
findings.failureMode: ClickZetta fallback LIKE retrieval fails because its ESCAPE literal has two characters.
findings.title: Use a single-character escape literal in ClickZetta quote mode

findings.description: With IRIS_TEXT_INDEX disabled, the helper escapes %, _ and backslashes with backslashes, but SQL declares '|' as the escape character. A search for '50%' sends '%50\%%' and fails to find '50% discount'; literal pipes also acquire unintended escape semantics. Use the same backslash escape character as the generated pattern.
findings.failureMode: IRIS fallback full-text search returns incorrect results for literal special characters.
findings.title: Match the IRIS ESCAPE character to the helper

findings.description: The 'not contains' branch now inserts backslash-escaped values but omits the ESCAPE clause used by the other branches. On MySQL with NO_BACKSLASH_ESCAPES, '50%' becomes '%50\%%', which does not match metadata '50% discount'; NOT LIKE therefore includes the document that should be excluded. Add escape='\\' to notlike as well.
findings.failureMode: The not-contains metadata filter includes forbidden values on MySQL with NO_BACKSLASH_ESCAPES.
findings.title: Declare the escape character for the negative metadata filter

findings.description: make type-check fails at this return: result.get('result') can be None, and the preceding guard deliberately leaves that value unnarrowed, so basedpyright reports str | None as incompatible with str. Reject all non-string results, including None, with TemplateRenderError before returning.
findings.failureMode: Confirmed make type-check fails with the sole reportReturnType error at template_renderer.py:40.
findings.title: Reject None in the renderer result validation

findings.description: The 23 newly added renderer tests pass graph=mock_graph, although neither TemplateTransformNode nor Node accepts graph. The Boolean test raises TypeError before reaching the renderer. Remove this keyword in all newly added constructors (Boolean through escape-filter; calls at lines 451, 484, 515, 545, 575, 602, 645, 687, 719, 749, 779, 810, 840, 870, 900, 930, 960, 990, 1020, 1050, 1080, 1110, 1140).
findings.failureMode: Invoking test_run_with_boolean_values fails with unexpected keyword argument 'graph'; the same correction is required at all newly added constructors.
findings.title: Remove the unsupported graph argument from new tests

findings.description: The 23 newly added tests pass node_data directly as config, but Node requires config['id'] and config['data']. Removing the independent unsupported graph keyword still leaves ValueError('Node ID is required.'). Wrap node_data as {'id': 'test_node', 'data': node_data} in each new constructor (calls at lines 451, 484, 515, 545, 575, 602, 645, 687, 719, 749, 779, 810, 840, 870, 900, 930, 960, 990, 1020, 1050, 1080, 1110, 1140).
findings.failureMode: The new Boolean test and parallel new tests fail node initialization instead of checking renderer results because config has neither id nor data.
findings.title: Pass a complete node config in the new tests

findings.description: The newly added reversed equality triggers Ruff SIM300, making the registered make check fail. Put result.outputs['output'] on the left and the expected string on the right.
findings.failureMode: make check exits nonzero on SIM300 at the new assertion.
findings.title: Use the lint-required comparison order

findings.description: Workflow execution persistence uses json.dumps with default ensure_ascii=True, so inputs and outputs containing `你好` are stored as `\u4f60\u597d`. Replacing the former unicode_escape conversion with raw keyword escaping makes a search for `你好` return no matching logs. Encode the keyword for the persisted JSON representation before LIKE escaping for inputs/outputs, keeping a separate raw pattern for session IDs.
findings.failureMode: Searching workflow logs for non-ASCII input/output content returns zero matches despite existing runs.
findings.title: Preserve JSON encoding when searching workflow inputs and outputs

findings.description: With IRIS_TEXT_INDEX disabled, the helper escapes %, _ and backslashes with backslash, but SQL declares | as the escape character. A search for `50%` misses documents containing `50%` because the pattern now requires a literal backslash followed by a wildcard. Use backslash in the ESCAPE clause to match the helper.
findings.failureMode: IRIS fallback search misses literal special-character queries because its SQL escape character differs from the generated pattern.
findings.title: Match IRIS's ESCAPE character to the helper

findings.description: The `not contains` branch now generates backslash-escaped patterns but, unlike the other branches, omits escape="\\". On MySQL with NO_BACKSLASH_ESCAPES enabled, LIKE has no default escape character: filtering out `50%` uses `%50\%%`, which requires a literal backslash and consequently keeps documents whose metadata contains `50%`. Pass the same explicit escape argument to notlike as to like.
findings.failureMode: MySQL NO_BACKSLASH_ESCAPES deployments return excluded metadata documents for not-contains special-character filters.
findings.title: Declare the escape character for negative metadata matches

findings.description: With tab swiping enabled on an iPhone, the right skeleton starts at the container's trailing edge and has width containerWidth - 32. This new anchor puts the toolbar's leading edge beyond its trailing edge (for a 390-point container, leading = 748 and trailing = 390), forcing a negative width and broken/offscreen toolbar layout. Restore leftSkeletonAddressBar.trailingAnchor for the leading constraint.
findings.failureMode: Swiping-enabled address toolbar is constrained to a negative width and moved offscreen.
findings.title: Keep the toolbar leading edge tied to the left skeleton

findings.description: When a page loads, newly inserted reload/stop and reader-mode buttons in trailingPageActionStack are set to alpha 0 by updateActionStack. This list now includes browserActionStack twice and never restores the trailing buttons, so they remain invisible and untappable in both animated and non-animated updates. Replace the duplicate entry with trailingPageActionStack.arrangedSubviews.
findings.failureMode: New trailing page-action buttons remain alpha 0.
findings.title: Restore trailing buttons in the alpha update

findings.description: For a supported .default() UX configuration (divider width 4), trailing actions with no leading actions now lose their divider, while leading-only actions add a stray divider after the URL. The divider is physically between locationView and trailingPageActionStack, so its width must still depend on trailingPageActionStack rather than leadingPageActionStack.
findings.failureMode: Divider visibility follows the wrong side's buttons.
findings.title: Base the trailing divider on trailing actions

findings.description: API v2 uses CommonJS Nest compilation, but @calcom/features exposes TypeScript source and this extensionless deep import has no JavaScript module at runtime. Loading the new controller in the production API fails with MODULE_NOT_FOUND. Import TeamService from @calcom/platform-libraries, where it is already exported and used by the organization invite controller.
findings.failureMode: API production startup fails resolving the raw source-package import; repository lint also rejects it.
findings.title: Import TeamService from the compiled platform library

findings.description: An authenticated user whose membership role is MEMBER passes RolesGuard with this decorator and can create a usable shareable invite link. TeamService.createInvite has no further authorization check, so the admin-only invite permission is bypassed (and the new non-admin 403 test fails). Require TEAM_ADMIN, as the existing organization invite endpoint does.
findings.failureMode: Non-admin team member generates invitations despite admin-only authorization contract.
findings.title: Require TEAM_ADMIN for invite creation

findings.description: Every new invite returns `invite-link-for-teamId-<id>` as token instead of the random token stored in the token column. Clients cannot redeem this value, it does not occur in inviteLink, and repeated requests return the same token. Return `newToken.token` (or `token`).
findings.failureMode: New invite token cannot be redeemed and repeat requests return identical token values.
findings.title: Return the generated token, not its identifier

findings.description: This reverses the existing link destinations: standalone teams now go to /signup, while organizations/sub-teams go to /teams. For an already logged-in standalone-team invitee, signup's getServerSideProps redirects to / without consuming the token, so clicking the invite no longer creates a membership. Organization invitees also skip the signup flow that establishes parent-org memberships. Restore `if (!isOrgContext)` so each context retains its working flow.
findings.failureMode: Logged-in standalone-team invitee clicks returned signup URL and is redirected to home without joining; organization subteams miss parent-membership setup.
findings.title: Restore the organization-context link routing

findings.description: A normal reader-mode tap (or a summarizer long press) dispatches showReaderMode, but this handler now selects readerModeLongPressAction. BrowserViewController therefore calls profile.readingList.createRecordWithURL instead of toggling reader mode. In a private tab, tapping Reader View now persists the private page's URL and title in the shared SQLite reading list without requesting a save. Restore displayView: .readerMode.
findings.failureMode: Reader-mode tap unexpectedly saves the URL/title, including private browsing pages, to persistent shared reading-list storage.
findings.title: Restore reader-mode taps instead of saving pages

findings.description: The switch now passes false when a tap would enable reader mode and true when it would disable it. Besides reversing the isEnabled contract, the existing ToolbarTelemetry helper assigns that argument to the is_private extra: an active reader-mode tap in a normal tab is now recorded as private. The nil-state fixture in testDidTapButton_tapOnReaderModeButton_dispatchesShowReaderModes also now emits isPrivate=true and fails its assertion. Restore .available: true / default: false.
findings.failureMode: Normal-tab active/nil reader-mode taps now emit is_private=true; existing middleware test fails.
findings.title: Restore the reader-mode telemetry state calculation

findings.description: On an active reader-mode tab, cancelling address editing or opening the menu/tab tray now passes http://localhost/reader-mode/page?... to cancelEdit. AddressBarState overwrites the article's displayURL with that raw URL, and LocationView uses config.url.absoluteString without decoding it, so the bar shows localhost and later edits expose the internal reader URL. Restore the reader-mode exclusion so cancelEdit preserves the existing decoded article URL.
findings.failureMode: Cancel editing on an active reader-mode tab replaces the decoded article URL with the internal localhost URL.
findings.title: Keep the internal reader URL out of address-bar state

findings.description: The helper now returns FileWriteError, but prepare_tools still propagates all five calls with `?` into crate::Result. crate::Error has no From<FileWriteError>, so Linux builds fail with E0277. Keep std::io::Result or add an explicit conversion at the callers.
findings.failureMode: Linux tauri-bundler compilation fails because ? cannot convert FileWriteError into crate::Error.
findings.title: Restore an error type convertible to the bundler error

findings.description: On an empty tool cache, prepare_tools calls this helper for a nonexistent AppRun path. set_permissions now runs before fs::write and fails with NotFound, aborting bundling without creating the file. The same problem affects every other missing tool. Restore the write-before-chmod order.
findings.failureMode: First AppImage bundle fails when chmod is applied to a tool that has not been created.
findings.title: Create tool files before setting their permissions

findings.description: The exists check was inverted. When the tools cache lacks linuxdeploy-plugin-gtk.sh, prepare_tools skips writing the embedded script even though bundle_project always requests `--plugin gtk`. Linuxdeploy cannot find the plugin and AppImage bundling fails. Restore the missing-file condition.
findings.failureMode: A cache without the GTK plugin reaches linuxdeploy --plugin gtk without installing that plugin.
findings.title: Install the GTK plugin when it is absent

findings.description: Pass 7 rather than 6 to rewriteClientCommandVector: the vector includes the command, key, KEEPTTL, FIELDS, count, field and value. With argc 6, newobj is omitted and every successful HINCRBYFLOAT propagates an invalid `HSETEX key KEEPTTL FIELDS 1 field`. Replicas reject it; AOF replay rejects it and loses the increment (reproduced as value 2.1 reverting to 1 after DEBUG LOADAOF).
findings.failureMode: Successful hash float increments are missing on replicas and lost after AOF reload because the propagated command omits the final value.
findings.title: Include all seven arguments in the rewritten command

findings.description: Restore the deleted `| HASH_SET_KEEP_TTL` flag. After `HSETEX h EX 100 FIELDS 1 f 1` followed by `HINCRBYFLOAT h f 1.1`, HTTL now returns -1 on the primary instead of retaining the expiration, in both listpackex and hashtable encodings. The KEEPTTL argument in the replication rewrite cannot preserve the primary's TTL.
findings.failureMode: Incrementing a live expiring hash field removes its TTL on the primary.
findings.title: Preserve the field TTL on the primary

findings.description: Restore `static` on addHashFieldToReply. All its callers remain confined to t_hash.c and no public declaration exists; removing static exports an internal helper, violating mandatory AGENTS.md rule 7.
findings.failureMode: Internal-only helper is exported contrary to the repository's mandatory encapsulation rule.
findings.title: Keep the file-local reply helper static

findings.description: The macOS image is upgraded but the setup step still runs xcode-select against /Applications/Xcode_15.2.0.app/Contents/Developer (lines 166 and 392). macOS 15 images provide Xcode 16 rather than 15.2, so this step fails before the build. Update the actual selection path in both public and internal branches, not just their display names (the internal image change is at line 322).
findings.failureMode: macOS CI jobs fail in Xcode selection before compilation on the newly selected hosted image.
findings.title: Select an installed Xcode when moving to macOS 15

findings.description: The patch == 1 condition enables BUILD002 exactly while this transition still has a 9.0.0 baseline. That baseline lists System.Text.Json for Microsoft.AspNetCore.AzureAppServices.HostingStartup, but the current net10.0 project has no such reference, so the 10.0.1 managed build fails with BUILD002. It also disables dependency-removal checks for every later patch. Exclude the first patch instead (patch != 1), then enforce the check on subsequent servicing builds with the updated baseline.
findings.failureMode: First servicing patch fails with BUILD002 against obsolete 9.0.0 dependencies, while subsequent servicing patches bypass the same dependency-removal guard; both are fixed by inverting the added equality.
findings.title: Invert the first-patch baseline condition

findings.description: Replacing the file-scoped declaration with a block-scoped namespace violates mandatory AGENTS.md rule 2. Retain the semicolon declaration and remove the added outer braces; quarantining the test does not require changing namespace syntax.
findings.failureMode: The changed C# source no longer satisfies the mandatory file-scoped namespace compliance requirement.
findings.title: Restore the required file-scoped namespace

findings.description: The new `== '1'` check runs BUILD002 exactly when the baseline is still 9.0.0 and the build is 10.0.1. For example, AzureAppServices.HostingStartup no longer references System.Text.Json, but its 9.0 baseline still lists it, so its net10.0 restore fails with BUILD002. It also disables the gate for .2 and later. Use `!= '1'` for the first-patch exception, so .1 can build while the baseline is updated and later servicing patches retain validation.
findings.failureMode: 10.0.1 restore rejects an obsolete 9.0 baseline dependency; patch 2+ bypasses compatibility validation
findings.title: Invert the first-patch exception in reference validation

findings.description: macOS-15 jobs still execute xcode-select against /Applications/Xcode_15.2.0.app/Contents/Developer (lines 166 and 392). That image supplies Xcode 16+, not 15.2, so the setup step fails before the build. Update both selection commands to an installed Xcode path when changing the image (both public and internal pools).
findings.failureMode: macOS CI setup fails with an invalid developer directory before running build.sh
findings.title: Update Xcode selection with the macOS image

findings.description: Replacing the file-scoped namespace with a block-scoped declaration violates mandatory AGENTS.md rule 2. Restore the semicolon declaration and remove the added enclosing braces; quarantining the test does not require changing namespace syntax.
findings.failureMode: Changed C# namespace fails mandatory file-scoped namespace compliance
findings.title: Preserve the required file-scoped namespace

findings.description: Disabling strict also disables strictNullChecks, which TanStack Router requires. Running tsc -b --noEmit now fails at createRouter calls with 'strictNullChecks must be enabled in tsconfig.json' and produces widespread route-parameter errors, so both validate:types and build fail. Restore strict: true; this also preserves the repository's required strict checking.
findings.failureMode: The frontend build and type-validation pipeline fail because TanStack Router requires strictNullChecks.
findings.title: Keep strict mode enabled to preserve the build

findings.description: Both this component and work-queue-status-trigger-fields.tsx:36 always write the selected status to expect. With 'Stays in Not Ready', entering Not Ready counts as an expected event instead of starting a stay-in-state timer. The proactive evaluator removes the bucket once that count reaches the threshold, so remaining Not Ready for the configured duration does not fire. Use the same posture-dependent after/expect binding as deployment status in both components.
findings.failureMode: The proactive status templates count state-entry events as expected events and fail to detect remaining in that state.
findings.title: Bind proactive pool and queue status to after

findings.description: Choose 'Enters Ready', switch to 'Stays in', and select Ready again. Changing the bound field to after leaves expect=['prefect.deployment.ready'] in the form. A subsequent not-ready event is not expected and cannot cancel the proactive timer, so the automation can fire even though the deployment left Ready. Clear or normalize the obsolete event filter when changing posture rather than retaining both filters.
findings.failureMode: Switching Reactive to Proactive keeps the old expect filter and yields a stay-in-state trigger that ignores departure events.
findings.title: Remove stale expect values when changing posture

findings.description: Clearing the textarea produces [''] because split('\n') always returns at least one entry. The form accepts that value, but the backend treats a nonempty expect set as literal event filters: [''] matches no real event, unlike an empty expect set which matches any event. Normalize a cleared textarea to [] (and omit blank lines) so deleting the filter actually removes it.
findings.failureMode: A cleared custom event filter serializes as [''] and silently stops matching events instead of removing the filter.
findings.title: Clear expected events to an empty array

findings.description: The new proactive Within inputs permit 1–9 seconds, and EventTriggerSchema accepts them, but backend EventTrigger validation rejects those values. Selecting 'Stays in' and entering 5 therefore produces an invalid automation trigger without a form error. Enforce a minimum of 10 seconds in the proactive input and validation; the same defect exists in custom (line 80), work-pool (line 95), and work-queue (line 95).
findings.failureMode: New proactive trigger templates accept and output a window rejected by the backend.
findings.title: Enforce the proactive ten-second minimum

findings.description: FormControl wraps the non-DOM Select root, so its generated id, aria-describedby and aria-invalid never reach SelectTrigger. The Status label points at a nonexistent element, leaving the combobox unnamed for screen readers and preventing label activation. Move FormControl around SelectTrigger in this component and the work-pool/work-queue status components (lines 42–47).
findings.failureMode: All three new status comboboxes lack their label association and form error accessibility attributes.
findings.title: Attach form control attributes to the status trigger

findings.description: When tab swiping is enabled, the right skeleton starts at the container trailing edge and has width containerWidth - 32. Attaching the toolbar leading edge to its trailing edge while keeping the toolbar trailing edge at its leading edge imposes a negative width. A 390-point UIKit layout probe collapses the toolbar to width 0 at x=390, hiding the address bar. Restore leftSkeletonAddressBar.trailingAnchor.
findings.failureMode: Tab-swiping toolbar has negative width and broken layout.
findings.title: Keep the toolbar leading edge attached to the left skeleton

findings.description: When a page loads, trailing actions such as reload, stop and reader mode are added with alpha 0 by updateActionStack. This list now includes browserActionStack twice and omits trailingPageActionStack, so neither layout branch restores those buttons to alpha 1; they remain invisible and untappable even with animations disabled. Replace the duplicate with trailingPageActionStack.arrangedSubviews.
findings.failureMode: Trailing action buttons stay alpha 0 after configuration.
findings.title: Restore trailing buttons to the alpha update list

findings.description: With the public .default() UX configuration and trailing-only actions, this check sets the divider width to 0 instead of 4. The divider is constrained between locationView and trailingPageActionStack, so checking leadingPageActionStack also inserts unwanted trailing spacing in leading-only configurations. Base this check on trailingPageActionStack.arrangedSubviews.
findings.failureMode: Divider disappears or appears on the wrong configurations.
findings.title: Base the trailing divider on trailing page actions

findings.description: After SelectLightTheme, the test now reads darkThemeView and expects "1". The dark option should be unselected, so the theme-change test fails on a correct Light selection. Restore lightThemeView for this assertion.
findings.failureMode: testCheckSystemThemeChanges fails when Light mode is correctly selected
findings.title: Read the light-theme button after selecting Light

findings.description: Moving `goto(NewTabScreen)` after the Done tap leaves the app on the Shortcuts settings controller when Done is queried. TopSitesSettingsViewController does not install a Done button; that button belongs to the parent Homepage/settings screens. The test therefore times out before checking that shortcuts disappeared. Restore navigation out of Shortcuts before tapping Done.
findings.failureMode: testDisableTopSitesSettingsRemovesSection waits for a nonexistent Done button on the Shortcuts screen
findings.title: Navigate out of Shortcuts before tapping Done

findings.description: Disabling strict also disables strictNullChecks, which TanStack Router requires. Running tsc -b --noEmit now fails at createRouter calls with 'strictNullChecks must be enabled in tsconfig.json' and cascades into route-parameter errors, breaking validate:types and the tsc build stage. Restore strict: true; this also preserves repository rule 11.
findings.failureMode: The app's registered type validation and build fail because TanStack Router requires strictNullChecks.
findings.title: Keep strict mode enabled for TanStack Router

findings.description: The pool and queue status selectors always write to expect, even when posture is 'Stays in'. With threshold 1, entering Not Ready satisfies expect and the backend discards that resource's bucket, so remaining Not Ready for the configured window does not fire the trigger. Bind proactive status to after, leaving expect to detect a later status change, as the deployment template does. The identical defect is at work-queue-status-trigger-fields.tsx:36.
findings.failureMode: Both pool and queue stays-in templates treat the chosen status as an expected event and suppress their own timer rather than starting it.
findings.title: Bind proactive pool and queue status to after

findings.description: Choose 'Enters / Not Ready', switch to 'Stays in', then select 'Not Ready' again. Switching the binding to after leaves expect=['prefect.deployment.not-ready'] hidden in the form; PostureSelect does not clear it. A subsequent ready event is then ignored, so the proactive trigger can fire even though the deployment recovered within the window. Clear or recompute expect for the proactive status configuration rather than retaining the previous reactive filter.
findings.failureMode: A reactive-to-proactive status edit serializes stale expect alongside after, causing a recovered deployment to fire a stays-not-ready automation.
findings.title: Remove stale expected status when switching posture

findings.description: Deleting all text produces [''] because split always returns at least one item. This passes the schema but makes the backend expect an empty event name rather than the default empty set (any event), so a cleared reactive custom trigger stops matching events. Return an empty array for empty text and discard blank lines.
findings.failureMode: An empty custom events editor serializes expect=[''], causing no ordinary event to match.
findings.title: Clear expected events when the textarea is empty

findings.description: Pasting a valid number-input value such as 1e2 is converted by parseInt to 1 rather than 100, immediately changing the displayed and serialized threshold. An interaction probe confirms the threshold remains 1. Use Number(e.target.value), as the other trigger fields do, to preserve valid numeric input.
findings.failureMode: Entering an exponent-form threshold silently sets the wrong event count.
findings.title: Parse the complete numeric threshold

findings.description: The new proactive Within controls allow values such as 5, and EventTriggerSchema also accepts them, so the wizard advances with a trigger configuration the server rejects: EventTrigger.enforce_minimum_within_for_proactive_triggers raises for 0 < within < 10. Enforce the server minimum in these controls and form validation. The same issue occurs at min={0} in custom-trigger-fields.tsx:78, work-pool-status-trigger-fields.tsx:94, and work-queue-status-trigger-fields.tsx:94.
findings.failureMode: Entering a five-second proactive window passes wizard validation but produces an invalid server trigger configuration.
findings.title: Reject proactive windows below ten seconds

findings.description: FormControl wraps the Radix Select root instead of SelectTrigger, so its id and ARIA props never reach the focusable button. Clicking the Status label does not focus the dropdown, and getByLabelText('Status') fails because it has no associated control. Move FormControl inside Select around SelectTrigger here and at work-pool-status-trigger-fields.tsx:42 and work-queue-status-trigger-fields.tsx:42.
findings.failureMode: All three new status dropdowns lack their visible accessible name and label focus behavior.
findings.title: Attach form accessibility props to the status trigger

findings.description: This new React component has no custom-trigger-fields.test.tsx alongside it. Rule 10 requires a co-located test for every component; trigger-step.test.tsx covers the parent and does not satisfy that per-component test contract. Add the missing test file so component tests can be discovered by the required convention.
findings.failureMode: Per-component test discovery has no custom-trigger-fields.test.tsx, violating the required component-test layout.
findings.title: Add the required co-located custom-trigger test

findings.description: This new React component has no deployment-status-trigger-fields.test.tsx alongside it. Rule 10 requires a co-located test for every component; the updated parent trigger-step.test.tsx does not supply that test file. Add the missing component test to satisfy the required test-discovery layout.
findings.failureMode: Per-component test discovery has no deployment-status-trigger-fields.test.tsx.
findings.title: Add the required co-located deployment-status test

findings.description: This new React component has no work-pool-status-trigger-fields.test.tsx alongside it, contrary to rule 10's per-component test requirement. The parent trigger-step.test.tsx does not supply that file. Add a co-located component test so discovery follows the mandated layout.
findings.failureMode: Per-component test discovery has no work-pool-status-trigger-fields.test.tsx.
findings.title: Add the required co-located work-pool-status test

findings.description: This new React component has no work-queue-status-trigger-fields.test.tsx alongside it, contrary to rule 10's per-component test requirement. The parent trigger-step.test.tsx does not supply that file. Add a co-located component test so discovery follows the mandated layout.
findings.failureMode: Per-component test discovery has no work-queue-status-trigger-fields.test.tsx.
findings.title: Add the required co-located work-queue-status test

findings.description: The vector contains seven arguments, but rewriteClientCommandVector consumes only the specified six, dropping newobj. Every successful HINCRBYFLOAT therefore propagates HSETEX key KEEPTTL FIELDS 1 field without a value. Replicas reject the update, and an AOF restart loses the acknowledged increment (verified: value 2.1 before restart became 1 afterward). Set argc to seven so the value is included.
findings.failureMode: Any successful HINCRBYFLOAT writes an invalid HSETEX without a value to the AOF and replication stream. The increment is not replayed, losing acknowledged updates on AOF restart or replica failover; panic configurations crash instead.
findings.title: Include the value in the rewritten command

findings.description: Removing `| HASH_SET_KEEP_TTL` makes HINCRBYFLOAT clear an existing field expiration on the primary, in both listpack-ex and hash-table encodings. For example, HSETEX h EX 100 FIELDS 1 f 1 followed by HINCRBYFLOAT h f 1.1 leaves HTTL at -1, so the field never expires. Restore HASH_SET_KEEP_TTL in the local hashTypeSet call; changing the propagated command does not preserve the primary's TTL.
findings.failureMode: HSETEX h EX 100 FIELDS 1 f 1 followed by HINCRBYFLOAT h f 1.1 changes HTTL from a positive TTL to -1.
findings.title: Preserve the field TTL on the primary

findings.description: All callers of addHashFieldToReply remain in t_hash.c. Removing static exports an internal helper unnecessarily, violating repository mandate 7; restore static.
findings.failureMode: The internal reply helper becomes an externally visible symbol in the built object, contrary to the mandatory encapsulation rule.
findings.title: Keep the file-local reply helper static

findings.description: Valid v2 configs store identifier at the root and bundle is an object, so reading bundle followed by as_str returns None. Mobile write_options then fails with 'app configuration is missing an identifier'; read_options also panics. Restore the identifier lookup.
findings.failureMode: Valid mobile configurations fail option exchange, and native build scripts panic.
findings.title: Read the original identifier from the identifier key

findings.description: An extension cannot be both json and json5, so all JSON/JSON5 configs now skip schema validation. For example, productName: "bad/name" violates the bundled pattern but is accepted by Config's ordinary String deserializer, instead of producing a validation error and exiting. Restore ||; deserialization does not replace the schema-only checks.
findings.failureMode: Invalid JSON/JSON5 settings bypass bundled schema checks.
findings.title: Restore schema validation for JSON and JSON5

findings.description: The replacement drops `config_metadata.inner = serde_json::from_value(value).context("failed to parse config")?;`. With a loaded config and a patch changing build.devUrl, merge_with returns success and updates TAURI_CONFIG/extensions, but the returned handle still exposes the old devUrl because value is discarded. Restore deserialization and assignment to inner, in addition to recording the extension.
findings.failureMode: Successful merge_with leaves cached configuration stale.
findings.title: Apply merged values to the cached configuration

findings.description: rustfmt --check with the repository configuration fails on this new statement and requires wrapping the expect call. Run rustfmt to satisfy the mandatory Rust formatting check.
findings.failureMode: Mandatory Rust formatting check fails at the schema initializer.
findings.title: Format the new schema initializer with rustfmt

findings.description: rustfmt --check with the repository configuration fails on this new insertion and requires a multiline method chain. Format this statement to satisfy the mandatory Rust formatting check.
findings.failureMode: Mandatory Rust formatting check fails at the extensions insertion.
findings.title: Format the extensions insertion with rustfmt

findings.description: An authenticated user whose team membership is MEMBER passes RolesGuard because TEAM_MEMBER is the declared minimum role. TeamService.createInvite performs no further authorization, so that user receives a usable shareable invitation link despite the admin-only contract. Change the decorator to TEAM_ADMIN; the new non-admin E2E case otherwise returns 200 instead of 403.
findings.failureMode: Authenticated MEMBER can create an invite without admin authorization.
findings.title: Require team admin for invite creation

findings.description: The controller imports the source-only features subpath instead of the compiled platform library. The API's CommonJS build preserves this package require, but teamService exists only as .ts in the features workspace; the Node 20 production startup cannot resolve it and aborts while loading the controller. Import TeamService from @calcom/platform-libraries as the organization invite controller does.
findings.failureMode: Docker/start:prod fails with MODULE_NOT_FOUND for the new TeamService source import.
findings.title: Import TeamService from the built platform library

findings.description: Every newly created invite now returns the fixed string invite-link-for-teamId-<id> as data.token, while the database and inviteLink contain the random secret. Clients redeeming or reusing the returned token get 'Invite not found', repeated requests return the same token, and both new admin E2E assertions fail. Return newToken.token (or the generated token) instead.
findings.failureMode: Every new invite returns an unusable token which does not match the inviteLink.
findings.title: Return the generated token, not its identifier

findings.description: This reverses both invitation destinations: organizations/sub-teams now use /teams, while standalone teams use /signup. For a sub-team invitee without a parent-organization membership, /teams only creates the sub-team membership; accepting it then fails when acceptTeamMembership updates the nonexistent parent membership. The signup flow establishes both memberships. Restore !isOrgContext so organization invitations retain the signup/onboarding flow.
findings.failureMode: Organization sub-team invite bypasses signup membership setup; acceptance fails on missing parent membership.
findings.title: Restore the organization-context routing condition

findings.failureMode: MembersAPI loading crashes because magic-link.js does not exist
findings.title: Restore the existing MagicLink module path

findings.description: The helper now returns FileWriteError, but prepare_tools still propagates all five calls with ? into crate::Result. crate::Error has no From<FileWriteError> implementation, so Linux tauri-bundler (and the CLI) fails to compile with E0277. Return std::io::Result again or explicitly convert this error into crate::Error.
findings.failureMode: Linux compilation fails because ? cannot convert FileWriteError to crate::Error.
findings.title: Preserve an error type convertible to the bundler error

findings.description: Every missing tool is passed to this helper with a path that does not exist. Calling set_permissions before fs::write returns NotFound, so a fresh cache fails on AppRun and missing GStreamer/output tools cannot be installed. Write the contents first, then set the executable permissions.
findings.failureMode: Fresh-cache AppImage bundling fails with ENOENT before the downloaded tool is written.
findings.title: Create the tool file before setting its permissions

findings.description: The GTK existence guard is inverted: an empty tool cache skips writing linuxdeploy-plugin-gtk.sh, although bundle_project unconditionally invokes linuxdeploy with --plugin gtk. Once the other tools are available, bundling fails because the GTK plugin is missing. Restore the !gtk.exists() guard (or always write the embedded plugin).
findings.failureMode: An uncached GTK plugin is never installed and linuxdeploy --plugin gtk cannot find it.
findings.title: Install the GTK plugin when it is absent

findings.description: cargo fmt --all -- --check fails on this new statement: rustfmt requires .map_err(FileWriteError::Permissions)? on a separate line. This blocks the rustfmt CI job and violates mandatory rule 3. Format the changed helper with the project configuration.
findings.failureMode: Mandatory rustfmt check fails on the newly added permissions statement.
findings.title: Format the new permissions error mapping

findings.description: FileWriteError is a new custom error enum with hand-written Display and Error implementations. This violates mandatory rule 8, which explicitly requires deriving thiserror::Error with #[error(...)] messages. Derive the error implementation and remove the manual implementations.
findings.failureMode: New custom error enum fails the repository's required thiserror compliance criterion.
findings.title: Derive the required structured error implementation

findings.description: The new GTK script uses four-space indentation throughout its functions and conditionals, while .editorconfig and mandatory rule 6 require two-space indentation for all files without a shell exception. This fails the repository's indentation compliance criterion; reindent the script to two spaces.
findings.failureMode: GTK shell source fails mandatory EditorConfig indentation requirements.
findings.title: Use the mandated two-space shell indentation

findings.description: The new GStreamer script uses four-space indentation throughout its functions and conditionals, while .editorconfig and mandatory rule 6 require two-space indentation for all files without a shell exception. This fails the repository's indentation compliance criterion; reindent the script to two spaces.
findings.failureMode: GStreamer shell source fails mandatory EditorConfig indentation requirements.
findings.title: Use the mandated two-space shell indentation

findings.description: The new adapter declares a str return but allows None through the guard and returns it. basedpyright rejects this as str | None, breaking make type-check. Reject None as well as other non-string results before returning.
findings.failureMode: Type-check failure from Optional return value
findings.title: Return only a validated string from the renderer

findings.description: All 23 added tests pass graph=mock_graph, but neither TemplateTransformNode.__init__ nor Node.__init__ accepts graph. Explicitly running these tests fails with TypeError before rendering. Remove this keyword from the new constructor calls (lines 455, 488, 519, 549, 579, 606, 649, 691, 723, 753, 783, 814, 844, 874, 904, 934, 964, 994, 1024, 1054, 1084, 1114, 1144).
findings.failureMode: New tests raise unexpected keyword TypeError instead of testing rendering
findings.title: Remove the unsupported graph keyword from new tests

findings.description: The new tests pass the flat title/variables/template dictionary as config. Node.__init__ requires config['id'] and hydrates from config['data']; after removing the unsupported graph keyword these tests still fail with 'Node ID is required.' Pass {'id': 'test_node', 'data': node_data} in all added constructor calls (lines 453, 486, 517, 547, 577, 604, 647, 689, 721, 751, 781, 812, 842, 872, 902, 932, 962, 992, 1022, 1052, 1082, 1112, 1142).
findings.failureMode: New tests have invalid node configuration and fail before execution
findings.title: Wrap new test data in the required node config

findings.description: Renaming this method to `verify...` removes it from XCTest discovery, so bookmark-to-Reminders sharing is no longer exercised when the suite runs. No caller invokes the renamed method. Keep the `testBookmarksShareNormalWebsiteReminders` name so the assertions still execute.
findings.failureMode: XCTest silently omits the bookmark Reminders regression test.
findings.title: Restore the XCTest test prefix

findings.description: `tapIfExists` waits on an `XCTNSPredicateExpectation`, whose first evaluation occurs after roughly one second. A 0.5-second timeout expires even if Allow Paste is already present, so the new handler never taps it; copy/paste tests still block on the prompt and fail URL validation. Use a timeout longer than the polling interval, or use `waitForExistence` for this short optional wait.
findings.failureMode: The added paste permission handler is a no-op even when Allow Paste is present.
findings.title: Allow enough time for the predicate expectation

findings.description: On iOS 17+, every iPad test and `testSelectBottomPlacement` now returns before both `app.terminate()` and `super.tearDown()`. Even a skipped bottom-placement test has already launched the app in setUp, so it leaves that process running after the test. Skip only the theme-reset operation, not the teardown cleanup.
findings.failureMode: Affected test completions leave the tested app running and omit superclass lifecycle cleanup.
findings.title: Always run teardown cleanup

findings.description: Renaming this method from testBookmarksShareNormalWebsiteReminders to verifyBookmarksShareNormalWebsiteReminders removes it from XCTest discovery. Repository search finds no caller, so running ShareLongPressTests silently omits the bookmark-to-Reminders assertions, also violating the required test prefix. Restore the test-prefixed method name.
findings.failureMode: Running ShareLongPressTests no longer exercises bookmark sharing to Reminders.
findings.title: Restore the XCTest-discoverable test name

findings.description: The iPad condition suppresses the Light reset for all onboarding tests, but testFirstRunTourDarkMode explicitly selects Dark on iPad too. That selection is stored in UserDefaults.standard, which ClearProfile does not clear, so the test leaves the device's app theme dark and subsequent tests inherit it. Limit the theme-reset exemption to the skipped bottom-placement case instead of every iPad test.
findings.failureMode: After testFirstRunTourDarkMode on iPad/iOS 17+, persisted Dark theme is not restored to Light and later tests run with inherited appearance state.
findings.title: Preserve the theme reset for iPad dark-mode tests

findings.description: On iOS 17+, every iPad test and testSelectBottomPlacement on iPhone returns before app.terminate() and super.tearDown(). This leaves the application running after the case, including when the iPad case is skipped. Guard only the theme-navigation step and always execute the existing teardown cleanup.
findings.failureMode: Onboarding tests finish or skip with the application still running and superclass teardown uncalled.
findings.title: Skip theme navigation without skipping teardown

findings.description: The list result's days must remain number[]. ListSchedulesPlatformWrapper passes each fetched schedule to getScheduleListItemData, whose Schedule parameter requires numeric weekday indices, so the new string[] declaration causes a TypeScript argument error on that existing path. Restore days: number[].
findings.failureMode: ListSchedulesPlatformWrapper fails type checking at getScheduleListItemData(schedule).
findings.title: Keep availability days numeric

findings.description: The server's IFromUser.id is number, but the replacement response declares fromUser.id as string. EventTypeCalendarViewComponent passes useAvailableSlots().data to useAvailableTimeSlots, which still requires IGetAvailableSlots; tsc now reports TS2322 at that call because these IDs are incompatible. Restore id: number in SlotInfo.fromUser.
findings.failureMode: Consumers passing the new GetAvailableSlotsResponse to shared availability hooks fail type checking.
findings.title: Preserve the numeric out-of-office source user ID

findings.description: Relocating Slot changes userIds from number[] to string[] in the public onTimeslotsLoaded contract. An existing callback typed to accept numeric user IDs now fails assignment to BookerPlatformWrapperAtomProps.onTimeslotsLoaded, even though this refactor does not change the ID representation. Preserve userIds?: number[].
findings.failureMode: Existing SDK clients with numeric-user-ID callback parameter types fail TypeScript compilation.
findings.title: Preserve numeric slot user IDs

findings.description: The new ./booker/types export targets booker/types.ts, but the package's files allowlist includes only dist, globals.min.css and fonts. npm pack --dry-run confirms that this target is excluded, so published-package consumers importing types from @calcom/atoms/booker/types cannot resolve the module. Package the type entry under dist and export its emitted declaration.
findings.failureMode: Published-package users cannot resolve the newly advertised booker/types subpath.
findings.title: Export a type file included in the npm package

findings.description: The expanded restriction also rejects unchanged QueryCell imports in ConferencingAppsViewPlatformWrapper.tsx and SelectedCalendarsSettingsPlatformWrapper.tsx. Biome lint now emits noRestrictedImports errors for both, and staging either wrapper will fail the pre-commit check. Migrate these imports to a permitted local/shared component before enabling the blanket ban.
findings.failureMode: Biome lint fails for existing atoms wrappers under the new import ban.
findings.title: Migrate remaining QueryCell imports before banning trpc

findings.description: A reader-mode toolbar tap (and the summarizer's reader-mode long press) dispatches showReaderMode. This reducer now emits readerModeLongPressAction, so BVC creates a reading-list entry instead of opening or closing Reader View. The separate addToReadingListLongPressAction still correctly uses that destination. Restore displayView: .readerMode in handleShowReaderModeAction.
findings.failureMode: Tapping Reader View adds to the reading list instead of opening or closing Reader View.
findings.title: Restore the reader-mode tap destination

findings.description: For .active (and the nil state used by the existing middleware test), this now passes true rather than false as isEnabled. Because ToolbarTelemetry currently writes that argument into isPrivate, normal-tab events now record is_private=true; the existing test expecting false also fails. Restore .available: true and default: false to preserve the post-toggle argument contract. The swapped extras in ToolbarTelemetry predate this diff.
findings.failureMode: Reader-mode closing events from normal tabs are newly reported as private, and the existing middleware test fails.
findings.title: Restore the reader-mode telemetry switch polarity

findings.description: In Reader View, cancelling address editing now dispatches the tab's internal http://localhost/.../reader-mode/page URL. AddressBarState prefers it over the existing article display URL, and LocationView uses config.url.absoluteString without decoding reader URLs. The address consequently becomes localhost, and editing again exposes the internal URL. Restore the reader-mode exclusion so cancelEdit retains the existing display URL.
findings.failureMode: Cancelling address editing in Reader View changes the visible article address to localhost and exposes its internal URL when editing again.
findings.title: Avoid restoring the internal reader-mode URL on cancel

findings.description: Removing private makes the underlying GleanWrapper accessible throughout Client, despite it remaining an implementation dependency used only inside ToolbarTelemetry; tests already inject their wrapper through init. This violates AGENTS.md rule 11's mandatory private access for implementation details and permits callers to bypass the toolbar telemetry API. Restore private let gleanWrapper.
findings.failureMode: The changed declaration exposes a previously private implementation dependency to unrelated Client code, violating the mandatory access-control contract.
findings.title: Keep the telemetry dependency private

findings.description: After SelectLightTheme, this now reads darkThemeView and asserts it is selected. A correctly functioning appearance selector deselects Dark when Light is chosen, so testCheckSystemThemeChanges fails with "0" instead of "1". Restore lightThemeView for this assertion.
findings.failureMode: The theme-switching UI test fails on a correct Light selection because it queries the Dark button.
findings.title: Check the Light button after selecting Light

findings.description: Moving `navigator.goto(NewTabScreen)` below the Done tap leaves the test on the Shortcuts subpage when it tries `app.buttons["Done"].waitAndTap()`. That subpage is pushed by TopSitesSettings and does not install a Done button; Done is installed on the Homepage/main settings controllers. The test therefore times out before reaching its assertions. Keep the back-navigation before the Done tap.
findings.failureMode: testDisableTopSitesSettingsRemovesSection waits for a nonexistent Done button on the Shortcuts settings subpage because back-navigation was moved after the tap.
findings.title: Navigate back before tapping Done

findings.description: For a valid config with a root `identifier` and an object-valued (or absent) `bundle`, this lookup makes `original_identifier()` return None. Mobile dev/build commands then fail in `write_options` with 'app configuration is missing an identifier', and direct Android Studio/Xcode script invocations panic in `read_options` at its expect. Restore the root `identifier` lookup so the RPC address file can be written/read.
findings.failureMode: Mobile dev/build fails and direct IDE build scripts panic for valid configs
findings.title: Read the original identifier from the identifier field

findings.description: A path extension cannot be both `json` and `json5`, so this conjunction disables validation on every JSON/JSON5 config. For example, `productName: "bad/name"` now passes the plain String deserializer despite violating the bundled schema's filename pattern, instead of emitting a schema error and exiting. Restore `||` so caching the validator does not remove validation.
findings.failureMode: Schema-invalid config values now accepted without validation diagnostics
findings.title: Restore schema validation for JSON and JSON5 configs

findings.description: `merge_with` computes the patched value but now drops it instead of executing the deleted `config_metadata.inner = serde_json::from_value(value).context("failed to parse config")?;`. Calling it on a loaded config with a different `build.devUrl` returns Ok and updates TAURI_CONFIG, yet the returned handle still exposes the old URL. Updating `extensions` does not update `inner`, which is what Deref returns. Restore deserialization and assignment alongside any extension bookkeeping.
findings.failureMode: merge_with reports success but exposes stale configuration for a state-changing patch
findings.title: Apply the merged value to the cached config

findings.description: The new schema initialization fails `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, which is required by repository mandate 3 and the rustfmt job in `.github/workflows/fmt.yml`. The formatter moves `.expect(...)` onto a continuation line. Apply rustfmt to this initialization so the formatting gate passes.
findings.failureMode: Repository Rust formatting check fails at the new schema initialization
findings.title: Format the schema initialization with rustfmt

findings.description: This insertion independently fails `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, required by repository mandate 3 and the rustfmt CI job. The formatter splits the `config_metadata.extensions.insert(...)` chain across multiple lines; fixing the schema initialization alone leaves this failure. Format this insertion as well.
findings.failureMode: Repository Rust formatting check fails at the extensions insertion
findings.title: Format the extensions insertion with rustfmt
